newsitem.title: UK: UK millenium fundraiser to earn millions - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK millenium fundraiser to earn millions - paper.

text.p: The man chosen to organise business sponsorship for Britain's controversial millennium celebrations at Greenwich in London could earn as much as 15 million pounds ($25 million) in commission, the Daily Telegraph said on Friday.

The paper said Mark McCormack, who acts as an agent to sports stars, could expect a fee of between five and 10 percent of the money he raises. The industry contribution to the project could be 150 million pounds or more, the paper added.
On Thursday Britain unveiled plans for a 750 million pound exhibition to mark the new millennium, promising it would be the most "thought-provoking experience on the planet in the year 2000".

The project, which was given the go-ahead last week by Prime Minister Tony Blair after a wave of adverse publicity over cost and content, will centre around a huge steel dome at Greenwich, on the banks of the Thames. REUTER AS ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
